key_insight: Cavity emission from two indirectly coupled qubits can be used to reconstruct the spectral density of correlated longitudinal noise.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a practical route to diagnose and quantify correlated errors, which is important for improving quantum error correction in scalable hardware.
method: Model two cavity-coupled qubits under correlated longitudinal noise without direct qubit-qubit coupling.
Analyze the cavity emission for white, quasi-static, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise cases.
Use averaging over many noise realizations, and for unknown noise types apply the convolution theorem to recover the noise correlation spectral density.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that noise-correlation effects scale as fifth order in the cavity-qubit coupling for white noise and third order for quasi-static noise, enabling reconstruction from emission data.
watch_item: Reconstruction depends on averaging over many noise realizations and may be sensitive to correctly identifying or separating noise regimes in practice.
paper_title: Reconstruction of the noise correlation spectral density from the cavity emission in a two-qubit system
